latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento 2.13, pp. 500-501]
english_translation: Since the Ideas can be perfected only when they are separated from what is alien to them, separated in effect from the as yet unformed chaos of Mind and returned to their source in the One, Mind must itself revert to God and unite with him. Thus Mind completes what Pico calls 'the first circle' (il primo circuit) of returning to its own first and final cause and to the Ideas' first cause, namely, to the unity of God.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico introduces the central cosmological principle of Book II: the *primo circuito* (first circle)—the circular motion through which the angelic Mind returns to its source. [VERIFIED] The passage draws on Plotinian and Proclean metaphysics: procession (*processio*, emanation) and return (*reditus*, reversion) form the cosmic cycle. The angelic Mind emanates from God as Ideas, but these Ideas must *return* to their source—not by leaving the angelic intellect, but by being gathered back into perfect participation in divine unity.

The philosophical function is to establish that cosmic circulation is the fundamental rhythm of reality. All emanation is simultaneously a return; all procession aims at reversion. The angelic Mind, first-emanated from God, immediately begins its return: the "first circle" completes what it means for the Mind to be perfectly creaturely. The passage emphasizes the perfection of the Ideas (*Ideae...perficiuntur*) through this circular motion—they achieve their full intelligible reality not as static forms but as dynamically circulating through emanation and return.

[INFERRED] This principle becomes the template for all creaturely reality: celestial bodies circle in their motions (reflecting angelic circulation intellectually), souls circle between descent and ascent (reflecting angelic circulation emotionally), human practitioners circle through analysis and synthesis (reflecting angelic circulation cognitively). Heptaplus describes the seven days as elaborations of this basic circularity. The Oration (O.1.12) describes philosophical practice as precisely this oscillation. Being & Unity grounds it metaphysically: all participated being exists through the soul's reception (procession) and return to the Source (reversion).
kabbalistic_elements: The circular motion of return parallels Kabbalistic doctrine of emanation and return (tzimtzum and restoration). The first circle prefigures the restoration of all things to Ein Sof.

other_texts: Plotinus Enneads on procession and return

notes: HARVESTER context: Introduces the central cosmological principle of Book II: the first circle of return. This circular motion becomes the model for all creation. Source: Allen, p. 6324-6326; Garin edition, Commento 2.13, pp. 500-501. Kabbalistic density: MODERATE (tzimtzum / emanation-return parallels).
